source.name: 4Chan Threads Text Archive Ten Billion 2009
source.short-desc: A text-only compilation of roughly 10 million unique 4chan threads, primarily 2006-2008, from an anonymous donor. Uploaded to the Internet Archive by Jason Scott in October 2018 under the archiveteam collection. The item ships the same corpus three times over: HTML, XML and MySQL.
source.capture:
SUPERSEDED BY archive_ten_billion_patched — DO NOT INGEST THIS, AND DO NOT WRITE THE XML ADAPTER. That item is the same corpus, repaired: it takes the chanarchive.tar.gz described below, fixes the single corrupt byte at offset 0x8cee0ac3 that garbles the posts table past a certain point, and republishes it as a mysqldump loadable by MySQL 5.7/8 rather than as raw MyISAM files. Everything this manifest could contribute, that one contributes more completely.

The uploader of the patched item states the relationship directly, and it matches the independent survey recorded below point for point: 'The XML and HTML formats in the original upload are subsets of the data in chanarchive.tar.gz (e.g. the XML version is missing /b/ and /p/; the HTML version is missing timestamps and post numbers, and its /b/ is corrupt; both are missing /con/).' The survey below found exactly that — 42 XML boards with /b/ and /p/ absent, and HTML whose number and date templates emit nothing.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND WASTED EFFORT: ingest is first-writer-wins on UNIQUE (site, board, post_no), so ingesting this subset BEFORE the patched dump would let its thinner copies win and permanently keep the fuller rows out. The order is not merely inefficient, it is lossy.

Marked dead-end rather than pending because the investigation is finished: this is not an adapter waiting to be written, it is a rendering that should not be read at all. The format notes below are kept as reference for anyone comparing the two items.

--- ORIGINAL SURVEY, retained for reference ---

22GB across three renderings of one corpus, and only the XML is ingestible. threads/xml/<board>.tar.gz (4.5GB, 42 boards) is one <thread> file per thread: <link> giving host+board+OP number, then nested <post num= date=> with optional <poster>, <tripcode>, <email>, <subject>, <text> CDATA and <img/> (always empty — this is the text-only dump). threads/style/fourchan.xsl is the stylesheet that rendered it and documents the full field set. threads/html/<board>.tar.gz (7.1GB, 44 boards) is that XML run through the XSL with the number and date templates producing NOTHING: every post is just postername + blockquote, so replies carry no post_no at all and no post carries a timestamp. It is kept only for /b/ (3.3GB) and /p/, the two boards the XML tree omits, where the OP number is still recoverable from the filename; the other 42 HTML boards are excluded as redundant. chanarchive.tar.gz (10.5GB) is the MySQL form, but as raw MyISAM table files (chanarchive/threads.MYD, ...), not a mysqldump — reading it means attaching the tables to a MySQL server, so no existing adapter touches it. It is downloaded anyway because it is the only candidate holding /b/ WITH post numbers. XML dates are minute precision with no seconds and no timezone ('2006-09-16 23:23'); they are presumably 4chan's displayed New-York wall time and would need nyWallToUtc like fybertech, but that is UNVERIFIED — cross-check a shared post against another archive before trusting it.

prepare.name: unpack the per-board XML tarballs
prepare.run: mkdir -p extracted/xml && for f in source/threads/xml/*.tar.gz; do [ -e "$f" ] || continue; b=$(basename "$f" .tar.gz); [ -d "extracted/xml/$b" ] || tar xzf "$f" -C extracted/xml; done

prepare.name: unpack the /b/ and /p/ HTML tarballs (the boards the XML tree omits)
prepare.run: mkdir -p extracted/html && for b in b p; do f="source/threads/html/$b.tar.gz"; [ -e "$f" ] || continue; [ -d "extracted/html/$b" ] || tar xzf "$f" -C extracted/html; done

prepare.name: stage for ingest
prepare.run: rm -rf out && (cp -al extracted out 2>/dev/null || cp -a extracted out)
